idea: Cremers and Weinbaum (2010, JFQA): when at-the-money calls are priced richer than puts, informed option traders expect the stock to rise, and such stocks outperform over the following weeks.
rationale_data: At-the-money call and put implied volatilities from the option chart model dataset (model category); their spread measures the deviation from put-call parity.
rationale_operators: rank() turns the spread into a uniform cross-sectional score; industry neutralization removes industry-wide volatility levels.

idea: An, Ang, Bali and Cakici (2014, Journal of Finance): stocks whose call implied volatility rose over the past month outperform, while rising put implied volatility predicts underperformance.
rationale_data: At-the-money call and put implied volatilities (option chart model dataset); their one-month changes capture option-market news.
rationale_operators: ts_delta() measures the 21-day change; the difference of the two changes is long call-volatility increases and short put-volatility increases; rank() normalises.

idea: Cremers and Weinbaum (2010): deviations from put-call parity reveal the direction informed traders take in the option market before the stock price adjusts.
rationale_data: put_call_parity_deviation_0 (option chart model dataset): the gap between theoretical and actual put-call parity.
rationale_operators: rank() makes the deviation comparable across stocks; industry neutralization removes industry effects.

idea: Xing, Zhang and Zhao (2010, JFQA): stocks with the steepest implied volatility smirk underperform, because expensive downside protection reflects negative private information.
rationale_data: 30-day at-the-money implied volatility skew from the option horizon decomposition dataset (model category).
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the skew across stocks and the minus sign shorts the steepest skews; industry neutralization compares within industries.

idea: Bali and Hovakimian (2009, Management Science): the spread of realized over implied volatility negatively predicts stock returns; options price in information that realized volatility has not shown yet.
rationale_data: 30-day realized close-to-close volatility and 30-day at-the-money call implied volatility, both from the option horizon decomposition dataset.
rationale_operators: The difference is the volatility spread; rank() normalises it and the minus sign shorts stocks whose realized volatility exceeds implied volatility.

idea: Gu, Kelly and Xiu (2020, RFS): machine-learning combinations of many predictors forecast the cross-section of returns better than single factors; this model forecasts 20-day returns.
rationale_data: short_term_return_pred_r20_q1 (multi factor market return predictions, model category): a regression forecast of the 20-day forward return.
rationale_operators: rank() keeps only the cross-sectional ordering of the forecast; subindustry neutralization removes industry bets.

idea: Event-driven return forecasts: corporate events carry information that prices absorb over several days (Ke, Kelly and Xiu 2019 on text-based return prediction); this model forecasts 5-day returns from event embeddings.
rationale_data: event_embedding_5d_regression_prediction (multi factor market return predictions, model category): a 5-day forward return forecast from event features.
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the forecast across stocks; subindustry neutralization isolates stock-specific event effects.

idea: A 5-day return forecast built to be weakly correlated with the main short-horizon signals, so it adds diversification (Gu, Kelly and Xiu 2020 on machine-learning return prediction).
rationale_data: short_horizon_hedge3_quantile1_5d_pred (multi-source market return prediction, model category): the predicted probability of a top-quantile 5-day return.
rationale_operators: rank() turns the probability into a cross-sectional score; subindustry neutralization removes industry effects.

idea: Jiang, Kelly and Xiu (2023, Journal of Finance), (Re-)Imag(in)ing Price Trends: convolutional networks reading price-chart images predict future returns beyond standard momentum and reversal.
rationale_data: img30d_return_bisection_prob1_zackbatch (deep learning chart-based alpha, model category): the CNN probability that the 30-day return is above the median.
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the probability across stocks; subindustry neutralization removes industry trends.

idea: Option-implied information predicts short-horizon stock returns (Cremers and Weinbaum 2010; An et al. 2014); this model maps option-implied features of large and mid caps into a 5-day return forecast.
rationale_data: predicted_stock_return_5d_tdang (option chart image return prediction, model category): a 5-day cross-sectional return forecast for US large and mid caps.
rationale_operators: rank() keeps the ordering of the forecast; subindustry neutralization removes industry exposure.

idea: Technical-indicator models forecast short-horizon returns (Brock, Lakonishok and LeBaron 1992; Jiang, Kelly and Xiu 2023); this field is the predicted 10-day return category from indicator set 1.
rationale_data: predicted_return_quantile_1 (technical indicator chart prediction, model category).
rationale_operators: rank() turns the predicted category into a cross-sectional score; subindustry neutralization removes industry effects.

idea: Short-term reversal (Jegadeesh 1990; Lehmann 1990): stocks that closed near the bottom of their recent trading range tend to rebound over the next days, because liquidity-driven selling pressure reverses.
rationale_data: williams_percent_range_10d (technical indicator chart prediction, model category): where the close sits within the 10-day high-low range.
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the indicator and the minus sign buys stocks near the bottom of their range; subindustry neutralization keeps the bet stock-specific.

idea: Volume-weighted short-term reversal: heavy selling on high volume (low money flow index) is followed by rebounds as liquidity providers are compensated (Campbell, Grossman and Wang 1993).
rationale_data: money_flow_index_10d_2 (technical indicator chart prediction, model category): the 10-day volume-weighted relative strength index.
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the index and the minus sign buys oversold stocks; subindustry neutralization keeps the bet stock-specific.

idea: News attention predicts returns (Fang and Peress 2009; Jiang, Kelly and Xiu 2023 for image-based learning); this model reads images of news-count history and forecasts the 10-day return.
rationale_data: prob_rank_bin1_10d_img_news (deep learning event return prediction, news category): a 10-day forward return forecast from news-count images.
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the unbounded forecast (and tames its outliers); subindustry neutralization removes industry news cycles.

idea: Drechsler and Drechsler (2014), The Shorting Premium: stocks that are expensive to borrow and heavily lent out are crowded shorts and underperform.
rationale_data: shrt7_combo_utilisation_x_rate (short selling model, model category): lending utilization multiplied by the loan rate.
rationale_operators: vec_avg() aggregates the vector field, rank() normalises it and the minus sign shorts the most expensive, most utilised borrows.

idea: Cohen, Diether and Malloy (2007, Journal of Finance): increases in shorting demand, visible as rising loan fees, predict negative future returns.
rationale_data: shrt7_combo_deltarate (short selling model, model category): the normalised time-series change of the stock loan rate.
rationale_operators: vec_avg() aggregates the vector field; rank() normalises and the minus sign shorts stocks whose borrowing cost is rising.

idea: Blitz, Huij and Martens (2011), Residual Momentum: momentum measured after removing common factor exposures earns about twice the risk-adjusted return of plain momentum and crashes less.
rationale_data: mdl68_ream_us_score (risk-alleviated momentum scores, model category): the risk-adjusted, standardised DREAM momentum score.
rationale_operators: vec_avg() aggregates the vector field and rank() normalises it; industry neutralization removes industry momentum.

idea: Chan, Jegadeesh and Lakonishok (1996): stocks whose analyst forecasts were revised up keep outperforming; EBITDA revisions are less distorted by accounting items than EPS revisions.
rationale_data: mdl354_group_pt1es_ebitda_ntm_r1m (comprehensive factor analytics, model category): the one-month revision of next-twelve-month EBITDA estimates.
rationale_operators: vec_avg() aggregates the vector field and rank() normalises it; industry neutralization compares revisions within industries.

idea: Deep-learning trend indicators extract persistent price-trend information (Jiang, Kelly and Xiu 2023); this field is one of the dataset's rescaled trend signals.
rationale_data: normalized_trend_indicator_2 (deep learning price signal dataset, model category).
rationale_operators: rank() normalises the indicator across stocks; subindustry neutralization removes industry trends.
